findings.description: Hermenejildo Patricio Cherres and Nicolasa Gavilanes had a son, Julio César Cherres, born about 1906, who died on 17 May 1908 and was buried at San Pedro, Guanujo, Guaranda, Bolívar, Ecuador; the parish burial entry names his parents as Patricio Cherres and Nicolasa Gavianes.

target_person.name: Julio César Cherres
target_person.death: 17 May 1908, San Pedro, Guanujo, Guaranda, Bolívar, Ecuador

supporting_sources: Ecuador, Catholic Church Records, 1565-2023 — burial entry for Julio Cesar Cherres, died 17 May 1908, San Pedro de Guanujo parish death register 1894–1915, entry 63, parents Patricio Cherres and Nicolasa Gavianes (ark:/61903/1:1:8HQL-MNW2)

1908 register page image (ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-G5JB-YX9), entry 63: "Julio Cesar... hijo legítimo de Patricio Cherres y Nicolaza Gavilanes" — image-confirmed the parish is San Pedro de Guanujo, correcting the index's auto-standardized event place of San Pedro, Córdoba, Bolívar, Colombia, which is a place-matching error (Colombia's Bolívar department also contains a Córdoba municipality)

Image reading licensed by calibration against two other indexed entries on the same page image: entry 54 Andrés Calunia/Caluña, whose page date (30 Apr 1908) matches the index exactly, and entry 55 Jasinto Carabajal/Carvajal, whose mother (Teodora) and date (30 Apr 1908) both match the index exactly; a third entry, 56 José Salazar, matched the index on mother and age but not the month (index gives 5 Mar 1908, the page reads 5 May 1908 — an index transcription error, consistent with the register's own chronological ordering)

The same page also indexes entry 61 (13 May 1908), María Victoria Cherres, legitimate daughter of Patricio Cherres and Nicolasa Gavilanes, died at age seven months, from Caspino (ark:/61903/1:1:8HQ2-1DW2) — Julio César's own sister, buried four days before him, not a different family; the index mis-records her mother as "Victoria Gavilanes," an indexing error that copied the child's own given name rather than naming a second wife. She matches tree person I3 (María Victoria Cherres Gavilanes, christened 5 Oct 1907), consistent with a death at seven months; two children of the same couple buried four days apart on the same page strengthens the identification rather than threatening it
